prompt:
Estimation question. Give an interval guess for the quantity below: the narrower the interval, the better, as long as the true value lies inside it.

Let the number of legal chess positions be $N$. Round $\ln N$ to the nearest integer.

solutions.title: Official value
solutions.body:
Official value: **103**. The number of legal positions is between $4.11\times10^{44}$ and $4.85\times10^{44}$, and $\ln(4.5\times10^{44})\approx44\cdot2.3026+1.5\approx102.8$, which rounds to $103$.

The paper asks for an interval guess; the scoring formula for interval width is not printed with the problem.

prompt:
Estimation question. Give an interval guess for the quantity below: the narrower the interval, the better, as long as the true value lies inside it.

The $2021$st largest prime.

solutions.title: Official value
solutions.body:
Official value: **17579** (the $2021$st prime, counting upward from $2$). Estimate: $p_n\approx n(\ln n+\ln\ln n-1)=2021\cdot(7.61+2.03-1)\approx17460$.

The paper asks for an interval guess; the scoring formula for interval width is not printed with the problem.

solutions.title: Official value
solutions.body:
Official value: **19283**, i.e. $n=\lfloor\log_22021!\rfloor$. Estimate with Stirling: $\log_2 2021!\approx2021\log_2\frac{2021}{e}+\frac12\log_2(2\pi\cdot2021)\approx19283.4$.
